notes: Curated catalogue. URLs point at upstream projects; RumiStack never vendors their code. Run `npm run verify-registry` on a networked machine to re-check every URL. Installers are typed (winget/npm) and allow-listed; everything else is manual.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.description: Anthropic's agentic coding assistant for the terminal.

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.description: Open-source terminal coding agent that works with many model providers.

tools.name: Codex CLI
tools.description: OpenAI's lightweight coding agent for the terminal.

install.note: Follow the official Codex CLI install guide; Windows support has its own notes upstream.

tools.name: Gemini CLI
tools.description: Google's open-source terminal agent for Gemini models.

tools.name: Aider
tools.description: AI pair-programming in your terminal, git-aware, works with many models.

install.note: Install with pipx or uv as described in the Aider docs (Python tool).

tools.name: Cline
tools.description: Autonomous coding agent for VS Code.

install.note: Install the VS Code extension saoudrizwan.claude-dev (add it under VS Code extensions in Device sync).

tools.name: FreeLLMAPI
tools.description: Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint that fans out to free-tier LLM providers.

install.note: Self-hosted service. Follow the upstream README; review its install scripts before running them.

tools.name: OmniRoute
tools.description: AI gateway/router that exposes many providers behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

install.note: Self-hosted service. Follow the upstream README; several forks exist, so confirm you are using the project you intend.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Python SDK and proxy server that unifies 100+ LLM APIs in OpenAI format.

install.note: pip/uv or Docker deployment; see the LiteLLM proxy docs.

tools.name: Ollama
tools.description: Run open models locally with an OpenAI-compatible API on localhost.

tools.name: Anthropic Skills
tools.description: Official example skills (documents, frontend design, skill creator and more).

install.note: Install skills through the Skills Marketplace view or your assistant's plugin system.

tools.name: Superpowers
tools.description: Community skills framework: brainstorming, planning, TDD and debugging workflows.

install.note: Installed as an assistant plugin; follow the upstream README for your assistant.

tools.name: Vercel Skills CLI
tools.description: `npx skills` installer used by RumiStack's Restore-Skills script.

install.note: Run on demand with npx (needs Node.js 22.20+); nothing to install globally.

tools.name: Context7 MCP
tools.description: MCP server that serves up-to-date library documentation to assistants.

install.note: Configure through the MCP Servers view; the client launches it with npx.

tools.name: Playwright MCP
tools.description: Microsoft's MCP server for browser automation via Playwright.

install.note: Configure through the MCP Servers view; the client launches it with npx.

tools.name: GitHub MCP Server
tools.description: GitHub's official MCP server for repositories, issues and pull requests.

install.note: Use the hosted remote endpoint or run it locally; authenticate with a token held in an environment variable.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.description: End-to-end browser testing for web apps.

install.note: Project-local: run `npm init playwright@latest` inside the project that needs it.

tools.name: promptfoo
tools.description: Test and red-team prompts, models and agents from the command line.

tools.name: Vitest
tools.description: Fast Vite-native unit test runner.

tools.name: Gitleaks
tools.description: Detect hardcoded secrets in git repositories and files.

install.note: Download a release binary or use your preferred package manager; see upstream.

tools.name: Trivy
tools.description: Vulnerability, misconfiguration and secret scanner for code, images and IaC.

install.note: See the upstream installation page for Windows options.

tools.name: OSV-Scanner
tools.description: Scan dependencies against the OSV vulnerability database.

install.note: Download a release binary; see upstream.

tools.name: Git for Windows
tools.description: Distributed version control; required by RumiStack.

tools.name: Node.js LTS
tools.description: JavaScript runtime; required by RumiStack and most assistants.

tools.name: GitHub CLI
tools.description: `gh` command line for GitHub; used by the optional publish helper.

tools.name: Docker Desktop
tools.description: Containers for self-hosted gateways and services.

tools.name: Visual Studio Code
tools.description: Editor with extension and MCP support; used by assistants such as Cline.
